long_biography.plain_text:
Gary Safady learned construction while attending Loyola Marymount University, working early shifts as a union labourer before evening classes. He later appraised commercial property and handled Kinko's real-estate work across 30 states. That experience showed him how site selection could become an independent development business, and he acted as general contractor on his first project to master the process firsthand.

His firm went on to develop dozens of retail and mixed-use properties across the United States. Projects included Louisiana Boardwalk in Bossier City, a riverfront retail and entertainment destination, and Bridge Street in Huntsville, planned around shops, offices, apartments, a hotel and a conference centre. The company's lean, self-funded approach let it pursue markets outside the usual urban centres.
